claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Selective laser sintering can introduce controlled porosity into HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing pores will reduce the overall density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Porous HfMoTaTiZr can retain sufficient load-bearing cross-sectional area to maintain its strength.
Pore-induced toughening mechanisms may help porous HfMoTaTiZr maintain mechanical performance.
Selective-laser-sintered porous HfMoTaTiZr can have reduced density without significant strength loss at room temperature.
Selective-laser-sintered porous HfMoTaTiZr can have reduced density without significant strength loss at elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The proposed material is applicable under both static and dynamic loads relevant to high-temperature structural applications.
The magnitude of density reduction depends on pore size, pore distribution, and pore volume fraction.
The preservation of mechanical properties depends on pore size, pore distribution, and pore volume fraction.
The hypothesis is rejected if porosity reduces density by less than 5% relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The hypothesis is rejected if strength decreases by more than 20% at either room temperature or 1000 °C relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says mechanical properties will not be sacrificed, while the rejection rule treats a strength loss of up to 20% as acceptable. This tolerance is not reconciled with the stronger 'without sacrificing' claim.
The boundary includes dynamic loading, but the proposed tensile and compression tests have no specified dynamic or high-strain-rate protocol, so that part of the claimed loading domain is not tested.
